source.title: Refusal-Gated Decoding: Preserving Refusal Behavior Under High-Temperature Sampling
source.authors: Phillip Howard; Xin Su; Allen G. Roush; Manikandan Ravikiran; Run-Yan Tan; Amir Abdullah

record.file_problem: None apparent; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices through Appendix J.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the single-direction finding as motivation for a residual-stream refusal readout, then uses a learned logistic classifier to route decoding. It reports probe and feature results, but does not measure the original difference-in-means direction or intervene on it to test mediation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports extensive decoding results, but those results test refusal-gated decoding rather than the claimed single direction. The residual classifier's layer choices and thresholds are not separate findings here; the refusal-prefix list and classifiers are components of the decoding method.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. (2024) only as motivation for a trained logistic residual readout used to route decoding. It derives no difference-in-means direction and does no ablation, addition or weight edit. Its probe AUROCs and SAE feature measurements describe refusal-correlated representations, not the causal mediation, transfer, or multi-direction structure any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that RGD raises mean greedy-refusal preservation at T=2.0 from 91.9% to 98.3%, keeps at least 98.1% of non-refusals on unchanged sampling, and adds 2.2–4.3% median latency; RGD-residual adds at most 0.5%. The SAE result is a side analysis, and the authors themselves state the logit lens does not identify a causal decision point.
record.recipe_differences: The residual readout is a trained logistic refusal classifier, not a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction; it is used to route decoding, with no direction ablation or addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Residual classifier layers and thresholds vary by model; the paper also reports changes in refusal-feature activity across sampling temperatures.

fits_no_version.finding: A learned logistic readout of the last prompt token predicts greedy refusal (validation AUROC 0.992–0.996, seven models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear residual probes at the last prompt token predict whether a model's greedy response will refuse.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, refusal-associated SAE features fire less often in early response positions at T=2–3 than at T=1, while matched control features do not change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-temperature sampling weakens refusal-associated residual features in early response tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: A harm-category readout at block 22 separates ten Aegis categories (macro AUROC 0.937); category information is already present at block 0 (0.903).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-grained harm categories are linearly decodable from the last-prompt-token residual.

record.problems: The residual-classifier results are validation-set prediction results, not causal tests. The SAE analysis is on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and uses feature selection and lexical refusal-opening criteria; the reported associations do not establish that the measured features mediate refusal. Refusal labels rely primarily on a 2-of-3 LLM-judge panel, with human validation on 50 responses.
record.rows_left_out: Decoding-method preservation, routing, latency, and dataset-label accuracy results were left out because they evaluate refusal-gated decoding rather than the claimed direction. The ten-category harm readout was also omitted because it does not compare harm judgments with refusal decisions.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction; no ablation, addition or capability check.
No jailbreak mechanism analysis or adversarial training against ablation. The temperature-driven feature decline is not tied to the refusal direction.
No affine, cone or multi-direction test.
The Aegis harm-category readout is not contrasted with a refusal-decision representation.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of a direction.
Reasoning modes were disabled; no reasoning-model test.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited once, as motivation. The study is a decoding-method paper. Its probe rows are the method's own classifier validation values and should be marked as selection or method values, not findings. The harm-category readout (Appendix J.2, Table 21) is correctly excluded from V5, since no refusal-decision comparison is made.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is derived or ablated/added; no general-capability cost of such an intervention is measured.
No weight edit or abliteration is performed.
No attack is tested as suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is conducted.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple causal refusal directions.
The harm-category readout is not compared with a refusal-decision representation to test separate encoding.
No transfer test of the claimed direction across languages, variants, or base/instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages for existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning-model test of the single-direction claim.
